newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CVRD advisor confirms gold, copper deposits-paper.
newsitem.headline: CVRD advisor confirms gold, copper deposits-paper.

text.p: A report by an advisor for Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) confirmed the existance of gold and copper deposits in northern Brazil, O Estado de Sao Paulo daily said.
The newspaper said the report by Canadian geologist Robert Mason revealed that the Carajas region in Para state contains an unusual number of world-class deposits.

"Continuous discussions led to the realisation that not only does the Carajas greenstone belt contains an unusual number of world-class deposits and prospects but also that it constitutes a unique fragment of the earth crust comparable only to the very best of the world-class mining districts," said the report revealed by O Estado.
The newspaper published fragments of the report.
Mason, who also advises gold mining firms in South Africa, Australia and the United States, visited Carajas region last October following a request by Vale do Rio Doce, the newspaper said.

Earlier this month O Estado de Sao Paulo said that CVRD had found "historic" gold and copper deposits in Para state, but the company denied the report by saying that it was too early to say whether drilling in the Carajas region pointed to a new deposit.

Vale's privatization, previously scheduled for the first quarter, was delayed until April to allow independent analysts to evaluate the gold and copper finds in the regions before the government sets CVRD's minimum price.
But officials have said that those finds were more likely to affect future mining concession prices and debentures on potential mineral discoveries than CVRD's net worth.
